clue.text: Reason why the greyhound punter is facing ruin

definitions.text: Reason why the greyhound punter is facing ruin

parts.words: Reason why the greyhound punter is facing ruin
parts.note: a gambler who loses at the racetrack goes to watch the hounds run, and the same idiom means heading for decline

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works both literally (attending greyhound racing) and idiomatically (deteriorating badly).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes falling into ruin, and literally describes attending greyhound racing.

clue.text: State where Roman huntsmen placed their trust

definitions.text: where Roman huntsmen placed their trust
definitions.meaning: Roman hunters trusted in the goddess of the hunt, Diana

explanation.surface: A question about where ancient hunters put their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN DIANA: Diana was the Roman goddess of hunting, so huntsmen trusted in her.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a US state in the Midwest, and split in two it reads as faith in the hunting goddess.

clue.text: Eager to enter the contest

definitions.meaning: being willing and ready, as in 'up for it'

explanation.surface: Someone keen to take part in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ready and willing is one sense; a match or sporting fixture is the other.

clue.text: Honour Ted in order to be compliant

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

indicators.note: putting the words Ted and in into order means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A man called Ted is given an award so that he behaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honour' looks like a verb meaning to praise Ted, but it is the noun for an award; 'order' is the anagram signal, not part of that award's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who obeys readily is docile and dutiful, synonyms of the clue word.

clue.text: Inclined to get one's shoes repaired

definitions.meaning: leaned over, as a ship does to one side
having new heels fitted to footwear

explanation.surface: Someone who decided to take their shoes to the cobbler.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that tilts to one side has done this; footwear given new heels has also had it done.

clue.text: Ignores compliments from the Underworld

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the name for the underworld itself
regards are good wishes, compliments

explanation.surface: Someone pays no attention to greetings sent from hell.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something is to take no notice of it, to overlook it.

clue.text: Was sorry for the first woman stuck in a grating

indicators.note: the first woman is lodged inside the grating, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a grid is a grating of crossed bars
Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone felt bad for Eve, trapped in a metal grille.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' signals that the first woman is lodged within the grating.
explanation.definitionFit: To have mourned or felt sorrow is to have been regretful, sad over something.

clue.text: Neither you nor I raise Cain

definitions.meaning: in grammar, not the speaker nor the person addressed but he, she or it
Cain was the third human in Genesis, after Adam and Eve

explanation.surface: An exhortation to cause trouble, addressed to nobody in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise Cain' looks like the idiom for causing trouble; here 'raise' only links, though Cain was also the first human raised as a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names he, she and they this way; in Genesis Cain came after Adam and Eve, making him the next human after two.

clue.text: Novel by a woman without a resting-place

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the woman goes round the resting-place

parts.note: a dame is a woman
a bed is a place to rest

explanation.surface: A book written by a homeless woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. The answer is George Eliot's 1859 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a George Eliot book, an example of a work of fiction.

clue.text: Son has desire to be smart

parts.note: a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: A boy who longs to look elegant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something posh and fashionable is chic, the sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Inspectors have splendid sunshades

parts.note: super means excellent, splendid
visors shade the eyes from the sun

explanation.surface: Officials who own excellent parasols.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseers who check work are its people in charge, synonyms for inspectors.

clue.text: Tree father planted in America

indicators.note: planted in says one piece is set inside another, as a tree is set in soil

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad planted a tree while in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planted in' signals a container, fitting the tree surface. The answer is a poisonous tree of Java.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Javanese tree with poisonous sap, an example of a tree.

clue.text: A prisoner such as the Vicar of Bray

definitions.meaning: someone doing time, serving a sentence

definitions.text: such as the Vicar of Bray
definitions.meaning: the Vicar of Bray in the English folk song changed his beliefs to keep his post under each monarch

explanation.surface: A clergyman compared to a convict.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray is the hero of an 18th-century English song who switched religion with each change of ruler to keep his living.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict serves time; an opportunist who bends with the times to keep favour is the other sense.

clue.text: Caustic man under unusual strain

indicators.note: in a down clue the man piece sits under the other, so it comes second
unusual says the letters of strain appear in an unusual arrangement

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A man under extraordinary pressure becomes biting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges STRAIN into ASTRIN; 'under' places GENT below it in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, biting remark is severe and cutting, which both words describe.

clue.text: Passing by in pleasing fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters of pleasing are reshaped

explanation.surface: Something going past in an agreeable manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Time going by, slipping away, is described by both phrases.

clue.text: Confined to bed with only the face showing

definitions.meaning: a card placed face upward on the table

explanation.surface: An invalid tucked in so that only their face can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone off sick is out of action at home; a card set down face upward is the other sense.

clue.text: Come to the point! Why won't the candle burn?

definitions.meaning: a taper is a thin candle, and it is off, not lit

explanation.surface: An impatient demand followed by a puzzled question about a candle.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle or narrow gradually towards a tip is one sense; a thin wax light that is unlit is the other.

clue.text: Pious man in extremely small dressing-room

indicators.note: in says the pious man is placed inside the other word

parts.note: very means extremely
St, short for saint, is a pious man

explanation.surface: A saint stands in a tiny changing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' and 'small' look as if they belong together, but 'small' is part of the definition. The answer is the church room where clergy put on their robes.
explanation.definitionFit: A church room where clergy put on vestments is a small robing room.

clue.text: As must be served up with a fruit

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the words are read upwards, from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A rule about what must accompany a dish at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' flips As and must each where it stands, read upwards in this down answer; 'with' then just tacks on the final a.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a kind of mandarin orange, an example of a citrus fruit.

clue.text: Transfer a large number into Saxon capital

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the city's name

parts.note: Hanover is the capital of Lower Saxony in Germany
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Moving a big sum into a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals a container. Hanover (Hannover) is the capital of the German state of Lower Saxony.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing control of something to another is a handover, a transfer.

clue.text: Token guarantor

explanation.definitionFit: A coupon exchanged for goods is one sense; someone who vouches for another is the other.

clue.text: Render a service partly to acquire rubber

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Doing someone a favour in order to obtain some rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'acquire rubber' is wrong: 'acquire' is no part of the answer's meaning, so 'to acquire' is the link and only 'rubber' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a rubber is the thing that rubs out pencil marks.

clue.text: Put right by a group of monks

parts.note: a set is a group
monks belong to a religious order, so they are in an order

explanation.surface: Something corrected by a band of monks.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange something tidily is to organise it properly, to sort it.

clue.text: Sport in Japan elecits total love

parts.note: a sum is a total
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A Japanese sport that draws total devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elecits' is the printed spelling of 'elicits', the link word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is Japanese wrestling, a national sport of that country.

clue.text: Little gratitude to firm producing tortilla

parts.note: ta is a British informal word for thanks, a small expression of gratitude
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company being thanked for making a flatbread.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a folded or filled tortilla, a Mexican snack made from that flatbread.

clue.text: Way to vanquish an egghead

parts.note: to rout is to defeat decisively
read as egg's head, the first letter of egg

explanation.surface: A method for defeating an intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but gives the head, first letter, of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: A path or course taken is a road or way.

clue.text: Pot-bellied and cantankerous

explanation.definitionFit: Having a big paunch is one sense; being easily irritated, quick to take offence, is the other dialect sense.

clue.text: Inevitable result of a golfing issue

definitions.meaning: an issue on a golf course, a matter of the course

explanation.surface: The unavoidable outcome of a problem on the links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that follows naturally is to be expected; a question about a golf links is the playful second sense.
